unit.why: A single anecdote about the Maggid of Kozienice weeping at Shabbat Bereshit Minhah, predicting a flood from a gematria of the Torah verse; the prediction comes true before Pesach.
unit.boundary_note: The final words 'ובתפלותיו הקל' are elliptical: the story ends with his prayers having lightened the flood.

stories.start_quote: שמעתי מש"ב הגאון ר׳ יוסף אבד"ק סעראצק
stories.summary_en: On Shabbat Bereshit the Maggid of Kozienice wept at the Minhah Torah reading and read the initials of 'קנים תעשה עצי גופר' as the year 573, foretelling a flood. Before Pesach the towns of Pilev, Kazimierz and Końskowola were flooded, and his prayers lessened the disaster.

tags.why: The tale is built on a prediction that comes true.
He predicts the flood and it happens.
The scene is set on Shabbat Bereshit.
The Minhah service is the setting, and his prayers lessen the disaster.

quotes: הלא קריתם ק"נים ת"עשה ע"צי ג"ופר
tags.why: He gives an exegetical reading of the verse by its initials.
He weeps over the coming disaster; this is not melancholy as a spiritual problem.
His prayers mitigate the flood for the region.

quotes: ששמע בילדותו מהישיש ר' איסר מפילוב
tags.why: The story is framed as passed down orally through named tellers.
